lines.text: Why does Diwali keep jumping around? Last year it was October 20th. This year, November 8th.
lines.raw: Why does Diwali keep jumping around? Last year it was October 20th. This year, November 8th.

lines.text: Because Diwali doesn't follow the sun. … It follows the moon.
lines.raw: Because Diwali doesn't follow the sun. … It follows the moon.

lines.text: Your birthday follows the sun calendar, so it's the same date every year. But most of our festivals follow the moon.
lines.raw: Your birthday follows the sun calendar, so it's the same date every year. But most of our festivals follow the moon.

lines.text: From one new moon to the next is about 29 and a half days. Twelve of those make only about 354 days.
lines.raw: From one new moon to the next is about 29 and a half days. Twelve of those make only about 354 days.

lines.text: That's eleven days short!
lines.raw: That's eleven days short!

lines.text: Exactly. So every year, Diwali comes about eleven days earlier.
lines.raw: Exactly. So every year, Diwali comes about eleven days earlier.

lines.text: Then why doesn't it end up in summer one day?
lines.raw: Then why doesn't it end up in summer one day?

lines.text: Because every two or three years, the calendar adds one extra month. It's called adhik maas. That pulls the festivals back into place.
lines.raw: Because every two or three years, the calendar adds one extra month. It's called adhik maas. That pulls the festivals back into place.

lines.text: It's like a watch that runs a little fast. … Every few years, you fix the time.
lines.raw: It's like a watch that runs a little fast. … Every few years, you fix the time.

lines.text: That's why Diwali always lands between mid-October and mid-November.
lines.raw: That's why Diwali always lands between mid-October and mid-November.

lines.text: You can see the difference with two festivals you know. Sankranti follows the sun, so it's almost always January 14th or 15th.
lines.raw: You can see the difference with two festivals you know. Sankranti follows the sun, so it's almost always January 14th or 15th.

lines.text: And Eid follows the moon with no extra month. So it keeps moving about eleven days every year, through every season.
lines.raw: And Eid follows the moon with no extra month. So it keeps moving about eleven days every year, through every season.

lines.text: And why that one night?
lines.raw: And why that one night?

lines.text: Diwali is on Amavasya, the new-moon night of the month of Kartika. … The night with no moon at all.
lines.raw: Diwali is on Amavasya, the new-moon night of the month of Kartika. … The night with no moon at all.

lines.text: The darkest night of the month… is the one night every lamp really shows.
lines.raw: The darkest night of the month… is the one night every lamp really shows.

lines.text: So next year?
lines.raw: So next year?

lines.text: October 29th, 2027. … About ten days earlier. Just like the moon says.
lines.raw: October 29th, 2027. … About ten days earlier. Just like the moon says.

lines.text: Question two! Why do we clean the entire house before Diwali? Every single year.
lines.raw: Question two! Why do we clean the entire house before Diwali? Every single year.

lines.text: Think about what just ended. … The monsoon.
lines.raw: Think about what just ended. … The monsoon.

lines.text: Four months of rain. Damp walls, fungus in the corners, that smell in the cupboards, insects everywhere.
lines.raw: Four months of rain. Damp walls, fungus in the corners, that smell in the cupboards, insects everywhere.

lines.text: By Diwali, the rain stops and the air turns dry. It's the first good time in months to clean, dry, and paint.
lines.raw: By Diwali, the rain stops and the air turns dry. It's the first good time in months to clean, dry, and paint.

lines.text: In our grandparents' time, homes had mud floors and lime-washed walls. Lime is a natural disinfectant, so after the rains, they washed the walls white again to fight the fungus.
lines.raw: In our grandparents' time, homes had mud floors and lime-washed walls. Lime is a natural disinfectant, so after the rains, they washed the walls white again to fight the fungus.

lines.text: Today we have paint and tiles… but the habit stayed. Our ancestors built it around how they lived, and we still follow it, because the timing still makes sense.
lines.raw: Today we have paint and tiles… but the habit stayed. Our ancestors built it around how they lived, and we still follow it, because the timing still makes sense.

lines.text: Shops do the same with money. … The old account books close, and new ones begin.

lines.text: So the cleaning isn't just tradition…
lines.raw: So the cleaning isn't just tradition…

lines.text: It's good timing. … And honestly, it's the only week the whole family cleans together.
lines.raw: It's good timing. … And honestly, it's the only week the whole family cleans together.

lines.text: Question three! My friend says her Diwali bonus is a gift from her company. Is it?
lines.raw: Question three! My friend says her Diwali bonus is a gift from her company. Is it?

lines.text: For a lot of people, it's not a gift. … It's the law.
lines.raw: For a lot of people, it's not a gift. … It's the law.

lines.text: India has a law from 1965, called the Payment of Bonus Act.
lines.raw: India has a law from 1965, called the Payment of Bonus Act.

lines.text: If you earn up to 21,000 rupees a month… you've worked at least 30 days in the year… and your company has 20 or more people…
lines.raw: If you earn up to 21,000 rupees a month… you've worked at least 30 days in the year… and your company has 20 or more people…

lines.text: …then the company must pay you a bonus. At least 8.33 percent, and up to 20 percent.
lines.raw: …then the company must pay you a bonus. At least 8.33 percent, and up to 20 percent.

lines.text: Because 8.33 percent is one month out of twelve. … One extra month's pay.
lines.raw: Because 8.33 percent is one month out of twelve. … One extra month's pay.

lines.text: And the law counts it on at least 7,000 rupees a month, or the minimum wage, whichever is higher. So even the minimum is about one month's worth.
lines.raw: And the law counts it on at least 7,000 rupees a month, or the minimum wage, whichever is higher. So even the minimum is about one month's worth.

lines.text: Companies have up to eight months after the year ends to pay it. Many pay it before Diwali, when families need it most.
lines.raw: Companies have up to eight months after the year ends to pay it. Many pay it before Diwali, when families need it most.

lines.text: That's why everyone goes shopping!
lines.raw: That's why everyone goes shopping!

lines.text: And how. … Last Diwali, Indians spent about 6 lakh crore rupees.
lines.raw: And how. … Last Diwali, Indians spent about 6 lakh crore rupees.

lines.text: That one season also created about 50 lakh temporary jobs.
lines.raw: That one season also created about 50 lakh temporary jobs.

lines.raw: Question four. … You know that photo of India glowing in every colour on Diwali night, from space?

lines.text: It's real satellite data… but it's not Diwali.
lines.raw: It's real satellite data… but it's not Diwali.

lines.text: It was made in 2003 by a scientist, Chris Elvidge, from years of satellite data. The colours show how cities grew over time.
lines.raw: It was made in 2003 by a scientist, Chris Elvidge, from years of satellite data. The colours show how cities grew over time.

lines.text: It is. … But for about one hour, it opens anyway. It's called Muhurat trading.

lines.text: Why can't Delhi breathe after Diwali? … Is it only the crackers?

lines.text: Crackers make it much worse… but they're not the whole story.
lines.raw: Crackers make it much worse… but they're not the whole story.

lines.text: Look at the timing. Diwali comes right when farmers in Punjab and Haryana burn leftover crop stubble.
